summary: Turn a screenshot into a spec: click two points for a caliper, tag each measurement as a size or a spacing, drag a guide to check alignment, then copy the whole set out as a text spec list. Every number below was checked against a capture whose true sizes are known.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Hover-to-measure is now OFF by default after this review; the other five measure flags are on.

try.do: Open the test capture in Photonz and press i for the Measure tool.
Click the left edge of the Save Changes button, then its right edge, then click again to place the caliper. It should read 124 px, which is the true width.
Measure the gap between Reset and Save Changes the same way. True answer is 12 px. Select it and switch Role to Spacing: it turns blue and stays blue for the next one.
Set Snap to Edges and centers in the tool options, then start a measurement in the middle of a settings row. The foot should jump to the row's vertical centre.
Switch the mode chip from Distance to Alignment and drag a guide down the left edge of the three labels in the second card. The middle one is deliberately 4 px out.
Open the inspector, read the Measurements list, then use its group menu and Copy as Spec List. Paste it somewhere.
Draw an arrow at the misaligned label, double-click it, and type a caption.
In the measure inspector Export section, hit Copy Image and paste into another app. Every caliper and caption should be baked into the pixels.

evaluate: Is the two-point caliper the interaction you actually want measuring to start from?
Is red for size and blue for spacing the right split, and should a gap between two elements auto-detect as spacing instead of you setting it?
Is the alignment guide worth costing a mode you can forget you are in, or would you rather eyeball two calipers?
Is the spec list the right shape to paste into a ticket, or does it need coordinates too?
rough: Hover-to-measure mostly does not work, and it has been turned off by default because of this review. It reads an empty field well (218x24 against a true 220x26) and gets almost everything else wrong: a 42x24 toggle reads as a 12x12 sliver of its knob, the Save Changes and Reset buttons read nothing at all, and a 624x44 settings row reads 490x42 because the walk stops at the label text.

That is not a tuning nudge. Preferring the strongest edge fixes buttons exactly but then a settings row grabs the whole card around it. Getting both right needs a different signal than the edge map alone, so it is filed as its own feature-sized task.
Alignment reports off by 5 px where the truth is 4, an off-by-one worth deciding about.
Deliberately left out: free-angle calipers, semantic names from text recognition, and the agent Describe specs button, all previously decided against.
The long-form version of this review, with every measured number and the reasoning, is in queue/audits/2026-08-23-measure-redline.md.
